key_insight: PEABF4 treatment reduces initial recombination at the electron transport layer/perovskite interface, but treated stacks degrade faster during thermal aging as losses extend into the absorber.
engineering_relevance: Depth-sensitive photoluminescence can help engineers assess whether interface passivation improves both initial performance and thermal durability.
method: Use multiwavelength excitation photoluminescence to distinguish interface- and bulk-dominated recombination.
Track recombination changes in PEABF4-treated perovskite stacks during thermal aging.
Interpret wavelength-dependent PL decays with diffusion-recombination simulations.
evidence_signal: PL measurements indicate reduced initial losses from fullerene deposition but faster degradation after PEABF4 treatment, with simulations supporting changes in surface recombination velocity and bulk lifetime.
watch_item: Depth assignments are model-supported interpretations, and the abstract does not establish quantitative device-lifetime gains or generality beyond the studied stacks.
paper_title: Wavelength-Dependent Photoluminescence Mapping of Depth-Dependent Degradation Under Thermal Stress in Phenethylammonium Tetrafluoroborate Treated Perovskite Solar Cells
